blocks.text: Look at that little girl. Taken from her home in Israel by raiders. Made a servant in a foreign house. She had every reason to be bitter. And she spoke up anyway, to help the man whose army took her. She knew there was a prophet in Israel, and she said so.

blocks.text: Thank God for servants with sense. If he had asked you to do some great thing, you would have done it. He just said wash.

verses.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Seven times down into that muddy river. Nothing on the first dip. Nothing on the sixth. On the seventh, his skin came back like a little child's.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: This story is full of the little and the low. A captive girl who spoke up. Servants who talked sense. A plain river. And a proud man who had to come down off his chariot and go under the water seven times. Church, sometimes what God asks is simple, and the hard part is our pride. Go down to the water.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to 2 Kings 5:1-14 (vv5-8 told in words); Elisha's word through a messenger read by the narrator; no healing promise.

cultural.note: The captive girl and the servants honoured as the wise ones; 'but' at the turn, a real preaching device.
